Symptoms: gateway slowed or failed as a result.
Resolution: the fault was removed and the incident resolved on its own.

097e93d1a96369c2d54086680da8359b1dc6b3b2.text:
search_document: DNS resolution failures
Symptom: connection errors naming unknown hosts across many callers at once.
Check the resolver's health and recent changes to records or search domains; cache negative answers briefly, not for minutes.

0ac90a2a85dcbbe3d282f0d89b8eb077d76f5150.text:
search_document: Postmortem: expired certificate on api.internal
The certificate of api.internal expired at 00:00 UTC; every call to it failed TLS handshakes. Renewal automation had been disabled during a migration. Fix: re-enabled automation, expiry alert 14 days ahead.

0e6c08c3829d7032efa0dc1c866d38b1a6d8e907.text:
search_document: Postgres lock contention
Symptom: statements waiting, lock timeouts.
Inspect pg_locks and pg_stat_activity for the blocking transaction; long transactions and hot rows are the usual cause.

2c89af7a0b45b9e3a5919c8d53e8b17747d693da.text:
search_document: Network partition between services
Symptom: timeouts between one group of services while each group is healthy on its own.
Check which caller-callee pairs fail, packet loss on the overlay network, and recent firewall or security-group changes.

2ec0292f0667f6f05341c5aae41f4ea93dda4f6b.text:
search_document: Postmortem: log volume full on a database node
Verbose query logging left on after debugging filled the log volume in two days; the database stopped accepting writes. Fix: log rotation, a disk usage alert.

3a302b87e7b53e137647f13d3cf948724c14f4d3.text:
search_document: Regression after a deploy
Symptom: errors or latency start minutes after a deploy finished.
Correlate the anomaly onset with deploy finish times per service; a deploy that finished within about 30 minutes before the onset, on the service whose spans dominate the slow traces, is the prime suspect. Roll back the version and confirm recovery.

3c6a885d0da164c1c278ac71056496e89d10cf29.text:
search_document: Slow database queries
Symptom: a database statement's duration rises; 'slow query' warnings.
Identify the statement from DB client spans, compare its duration with the baseline, check for missing indexes, lock waits and plan changes after a deploy or a data change. A single slow statement on the request path shows up as latency in every caller above it.

535566f781eac9a29fecc80987c396bac82a4e47.text:
search_document: CPU saturation and noisy neighbours
Symptom: services slow down together with no error and no dependency explaining it.
Check CPU throttling and host-level usage: another workload on the same host or core can starve services without any trace connecting them. Telemetry from the services themselves will not name the neighbour; host metrics will.

53797ce4318182c89879280f636ae882ac40bdd0.text:
search_document: Clock skew
Symptom: token validation failures or out-of-order events on one host.
Check NTP synchronisation; reject skew beyond a small tolerance.

56e664fc240b3ff87f8b189bd8101c1cf229ef56.text:
search_document: Disk full
Symptom: write failures and crashes on one node.
Find the largest growing directory (logs, temp files, a database volume); rotate or expand, then add a usage alert at 80 percent.

5a7d368b016a9550cf376c115530e940da52dd7c.text:
search_document: Blocked event loop
Symptom: an async service's latency rises for every endpoint at once while CPU is busy.
A synchronous, CPU-heavy step (a large scan, serialisation, hashing) on the event loop stalls all concurrent requests. Profile, move the work off the loop.

5aa2b3edab9de1ec3eb1110bededddd991d1c117.text:
search_document: Third-party dependency outage
Symptom: calls to an external provider time out or fail; 'provider charge failed' warnings; retries.
Confirm with client spans to the provider (peer.service) and their error status. Check the provider's status page. Mitigate with circuit breaking and shorter timeouts; retries without backoff make it worse.

656e522e52f9f5b9c1f55797831c6622d86eb421.text:

6732fa7d426e44081e03e25f48bbf7ef568da224.text:
search_document: CPU throttling under a container quota
Symptom: latency rises on one service while its CPU use stays flat at its limit and throttled periods climb.
A CPU quota (cgroup cpu.max) lower than the workload needs makes the scheduler pause the container each period. Compare container.cpu.throttled with latency; raise or remove the quota.

696a0a5a37c6a3aab3b7899364f6ef114f7764d4.text:
search_document: Retry storms
Symptom: call volume to a dependency multiplies while it is failing; caller CPU rises.
Retries without backoff and jitter amplify a partial failure into overload. Identify the retrying caller from attempt counters and client spans; cap retries, add exponential backoff and a retry budget.

70f33b3aee6832aa515b29577cb6bdcac853cbc7.text:
search_document: Bad feature flag rollout
Symptom: errors start right after a flag change, with no deploy.
Correlate the onset with the flag service's change log and the configuration reload lines; turn the flag off and confirm recovery.

9abe0305c3d44fcb489d7c627055a576e805fdca.text:
search_document: Database connection pool exhaustion
Symptom: 'pool acquire timeout' errors, requests waiting for a connection, db.pool.wait rising.
Causes: a pool configured too small, connections held by slow queries, or leaked connections. Check pool size against concurrency, the slowest statements holding connections, and whether callers retry and multiply the load. Callers that retry on timeouts turn a pool problem into a retry storm upstream.

9f38bd039184710aee50ac79d8ae660cb3d83b84.text:

Root cause: inventory's database connection pool was exhausted (pool size 1); requests timed out waiting for a connection and payments retried them, multiplying the load.
Symptoms: payments, orders, gateway slowed or failed as a result.
Resolution: the fault was removed and the incident resolved on its own.

a2e1a92b3d95f10ffb312b2e6e352a16c6e15acc.text:
search_document: Connection refused by a dependency
Symptom: callers log ConnectError / Errno 111 for one dependency, often in bursts, with no matching server spans.
The dependency's listener is not accepting connections: a crash-looping worker, a full accept backlog, or a port change. Check the dependency's restarts and readiness, and whether every caller sees the refusals at the same moments.

a3ac1bb72109601e9a2fcdc2f7332374d452fc60.text:
search_document: Cache stampede
Symptom: database load spikes when many cache entries expire at once.
Look for aligned TTLs or a cache flush just before the spike. Add jittered expiry and request coalescing.

a66e90a10a4d3a64b8988e71f99aa3e3a2ed3707.text:
search_document: Postmortem: memory leak incident (memory_leak_001)
Incident on gateway opened 2026-10-18 23:33:47.378015+00:00 (47 s after the fault began).
Root cause: an unbounded cache in payments grew without limit; memory rose and every request slowed.
Symptoms: orders, gateway slowed or failed as a result.
Resolution: the fault was removed and the incident resolved on its own.

ae03e76743a970d159ccfaf22b60bb5d27164baa.text:
search_document: Spike in 5xx errors
Symptom: the share of 5xx responses jumps.
Find the deepest service returning 5xx in the failing traces; upstream services usually just propagate it (502/503). Read that service's ERROR logs around the onset; an exception repeated with the same message after a deploy usually means a code regression. Roll back first, investigate second.

ae47bfca45ad5bd1c585a62b1eb0de0ef847829b.text:
search_document: High request latency at the edge
Symptom: p95 latency at the gateway rises above its baseline.
First look at traces of slow requests: find the child span that holds most of the parent's time; that service is where to dig. Compare its latency, error rate, CPU and memory against the last hour. Check for a deploy shortly before the rise. Latency that rises in every service at once, with no dominant child span, points at shared infrastructure or load, not one service.

b3a6e4d602bbe03afee5af87ec39e65a40a7fd5e.text:
search_document: Container killed for memory (OOM)
Symptom: a service restarts with exit code 137, its memory near the limit just before.
Find what grew (caches, buffers, request bodies), cap it, or raise the limit; an unbounded in-process cache is a common cause.

b734274560899225c9b292869b12130cb0ea48d8.text:

b9826a79b95989b7c722d9126f70d04b8ede00a3.text:
search_document: ClickHouse: too many parts
Symptom: inserts rejected with TOO_MANY_PARTS.
Inserts are too small or too frequent; batch them (seconds, thousands of rows) and check merges are keeping up.

bb35d29df9e5dd1bc0145818dfd81e95e788dc4a.text:
search_document: Rate limiting (429s)
Symptom: 429 responses from a dependency.
Check the client's request rate against its quota; spread bursts, honour Retry-After.

bc1938eac88314d3233ea81685629a534424a6ef.text:
search_document: Configuration drift
Symptom: one instance behaves differently from its peers.
Diff its configuration and environment against a healthy instance; redeploy from the source of truth.

c2aa6ade138e866cc3b13198a6349e82e16c7913.text:
search_document: Postmortem: internal DNS resolver outage
The internal resolver's upstream was removed during a network change. New connections across all services failed with unknown-host errors for nine minutes; existing pooled connections kept working, which hid the scope. Root cause: resolver configuration. Fix: two resolvers, change review.

c9d25d2b53bf524c6b780b1073d882eca6e1c3dc.text:
search_document: Kafka consumer lag
Symptom: consumer group lag grows.
Compare consume rate with produce rate per partition; a slow processing step or a hot partition caps throughput. Scale consumers up to the partition count; beyond that, add partitions.

d347848b6fa7a120efc261092c5f2a7d386147c1.text:
search_document: Long garbage-collection pauses
Symptom: periodic latency spikes on one service, heap close to its limit.
Large live heaps make collections long. Reduce allocation, cap caches, or give the heap more headroom.

search_document: Memory leak and GC pressure
Symptom: a service's memory grows steadily without levelling off; latency creeps up as it grows.
Confirm with container memory over the last hours. Leaks often come from unbounded caches or accumulating references. A restart is the immediate mitigation; find the growing structure with a heap profile.

eb59407c95b5739c46fe8e8a18b00c50b328c9bf.text:
search_document: Worker or thread pool starvation
Symptom: latency climbs and requests queue while CPU stays low.
Blocking calls hold every worker of an async server or thread pool. Find the blocking call in the slow spans and move it off the request path or into a bounded executor.

search_document: Load balancer sending traffic to bad instances
Symptom: a fraction of requests fail on one route while others succeed.
An instance that fails health checks still receives traffic, or a stale target remains registered. Compare failures per instance and the target group's health.

f36c5c313cf91e1c125b259d9b6648fe129d5c89.text:
search_document: Postmortem: cache stampede after a TTL change
A config change aligned all product cache TTLs to the hour. At each hour boundary the catalogue database received the full read load at once; p95 latency at the edge tripled for two minutes, three times. Root cause: aligned expiry. Fix: jittered TTLs and request coalescing.

fc2f7f5bc70e99a8fa694be3ed0ac670f83738b8.text:
search_document: Postmortem: retry storm from aggressive client timeouts
A client library upgrade lowered the default timeout to 200 ms and enabled three immediate retries. During a brief slowdown of the search service, callers tripled its request rate and kept it overloaded for twenty minutes after the original slowdown ended. Root cause: retries without backoff. Fix: exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget.
